A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, benchmarks, research questions, and analytical framework. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original embedding-clustering experiments, human-typicality correlations, compression analyses, and OLMo training-checkpoint results.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds multilingual evaluations, model comparisons, and further robustness and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains embedding extraction with average pooling, k-means clustering, item-to-category-name cosine similarities, and the same complexity-plus-distortion objective. Expanded explanations and additional diagnostics do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: v6 Appendix G adds evaluations using Spanish, German, Italian, and Russian translations across all three research questions. This substantially extends input-language coverage beyond v4's English evaluations, while retaining the original human categorization benchmarks.

E2.justification: v6 adds five DeepSeek-R1 distilled models to reported comparisons, including Figures 2, 3, and 8. Figure 24 introduces Pythia and Cerebras comparisons alongside GPT and T5, and Figure 11 includes multilingual BERT. These additions materially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include translated-input testing and the reported training-data-matched comparison in Appendix L. Additional measurements include FLOPs per token, effective rank, Gini coefficient, Hoyer sparsity, and distortion/complexity ratios. The original category-matched K, peak-AMI layer selection, and main beta=1 setting remain.

E4.justification: v6 adds clustering-seed robustness, computational-cost analysis, multilingual scaling analysis, training-data confound checks, and rank/sparsity/L trajectories during training. Appendix R also adds ratio plots described as beta sensitivity, although Figure 29 uses K on its horizontal axes, leaving that interpretation unresolved.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports averaging over 100 random k-means initializations. v6 omits that count but adds seed-specific AMI comparisons in Figure 9 without identifying the seeds or a replacement run count. This changes uncertainty documentation without establishing increased or decreased runs; existing table significance reporting remains.

E6.justification: v6 adds substantial results, including DeepSeek peak AMIs of approximately 0.36–0.46, positive model-size trends for non-English AMI, and decreasing effective rank with increasing sparsity during training. Additional seed, computational-cost, and matched-family results are reported. Numerical entries in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix R introduces the distortion-to-complexity ratio as an additional defined diagnostic. The core L objective, mutual-information and variance definitions, and singleton/one-cluster derivations remain mathematically unchanged between v4 Appendix A.12 and v6 Appendix P. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central compression-versus-semantic-richness thesis remains. v6 strengthens the implication that understanding and generation require distinct representational mechanisms and elevates existing training-dynamics findings into headline contributions. Section 5.3 also strengthens lower-L superiority from 'most tested K' to 'all tested K.'

C2.justification: v6 adds substantive qualifications that its metrics are proxies rather than direct measures of human conceptual reasoning, discusses compatibility with alternative concept theories, and proposes specific cognitive inductive biases. It also adds explanations linking multilingual scaling to training-data exposure and emergent capabilities to representational reorganization.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix A.1 supplies a direct dataset-access URL; v6 Appendix C replaces it with an anonymity and supplementary-material placeholder. v6 adds a promise to release code upon acceptance, DeepSeek model identifiers, and the translation API used. Existing prompt, pooling, and checkpoint details largely remain.

R1.justification: v6 adds discussion of Zaslavsky's color-naming and semantic-category work and distinguishes its embedding analysis from Wu et al.'s behavioral abstraction study. It adds the DeepSeek reference and removes several citations, including Barrault and Wolff. The broader positioning between cognitive information theory and LLM conceptual analysis remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, framework explanation, empirical narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Training dynamics receives a dedicated Section 5.4, ethics and reproducibility statements are added, and the former Appendix A subsections are reorganized into separate lettered appendices.

P2.justification: v6 adds a workflow diagram and numerous analysis plots, combines categorical alignment and typicality in Figure 2, revises legends and captions, and substantially relocates appendix figures and tables. Some displays are reused: v4's full OLMo trajectory appears twice in v6, as Figures 15 and 17.

improvement.justification: Multilingual coverage, additional diagnostics, and explicit proxy limitations potentially strengthen v6. However, important additions have unresolved reporting problems: Figure 29 claims beta sensitivity while plotting K, and Section 5.3 claims lower L at all K although Figure 3b crosses the human baseline. The direct dataset link and explicit initialization count also disappear. These reliability and reproducibility losses limit the added evidence's value, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
